name: Practice limits (new CBA)
title: The 2011 agreement limits full-pads practice
text: The collective bargaining agreement that ended the 2011 lockout capped padded practices at 14 in the regular season, ended two-a-days in camp and shortened the offseason program. Coaches predicted more soft-tissue injuries from under-conditioned players; a study of 2007 to 2016 injury reports found no sustained rise it could attribute to the rule.

name: First IR return rule
title: One player a year may return from injured reserve
text: Until 2012 a player placed on injured reserve was finished for the season, so teams kept hurt players on the active roster and listed them Out for weeks. From 2012 one player a season could be designated to return, two from 2017, and after 2020 an unlimited number after three games. Each change moved injuries from the weekly report onto the reserve list, which is why this page counts both.

name: Concussion settlement
title: The league settles the concussion lawsuits
text: The NFL agreed to a settlement, initially $765 million and later uncapped, with more than 4,500 former players who sued over the long-term effects of head injuries. It came with the concussion protocol, independent neurologists on the sideline and spotters in the booth, all of which turn hits that were once played through into weeks missed.

name: 'Probable' dropped
title: The injury report loses its 'Probable' line
text: For 2016 the league removed the Probable designation, which had meant a player was virtually certain to play, and tightened the rules on reporting practice participation. Any count built on the weekly report changes character at this line: Questionable became the catch-all, and teams were fined for leaving players off.

name: CTE in 110 of 111
title: Boston University finds CTE in 110 of 111 former NFL players
text: A study in the Journal of the American Medical Association examined the donated brains of 202 former football players and found chronic traumatic encephalopathy in 110 of the 111 who had played in the NFL. The sample was self-selected, as the authors said, but the number reset the public argument about head injuries.

name: Helmet rule, kickoff changes
title: Lowering the helmet becomes a foul; the kickoff is redesigned
text: Owners made it a 15-yard penalty to lower the head to initiate contact with the helmet, and rewrote the kickoff to remove running starts and wedge blocks. The kickoff had produced concussions at about five times the rate of an ordinary play.

name: COVID season
title: A season with no preseason games and a COVID reserve list
text: The 2020 season was played with no preseason games and a virtual offseason. Injured reserve was opened up so that any number of players could return after three weeks, a change made permanent in 2021, and a separate COVID reserve list was created. The reserve counts for 2020 include that list; it cannot be separated in the roster data for that year.

name: 17th game
title: The regular season grows to 17 games
text: Owners added a 17th regular-season game and an 18th week from 2021, the first change to the season's length since 1978. More games means more exposures, which is why this page shows injuries per team per week rather than per season.

name: Concussion protocol tightened
title: After Tua Tagovailoa, the protocol adds 'ataxia'
text: Four days after Tagovailoa was carried off in Cincinnati, having been cleared to play the previous week after a hit that left him stumbling, the league and the players' union added ataxia, any abnormality of balance or motor coordination, to the list of signs that end a player's game. Concussions are now more likely to be diagnosed and to cost time.

name: Dynamic kickoff
title: The kickoff is rebuilt again
text: Owners adopted the 'dynamic kickoff', with the coverage team lined up at the receiving team's 40 and no running start, to bring returns back without the collisions. Returns rose by more than a thousand plays in 2025; the league reports a 35 percent lower rate of lower-body injury on the play than under the old format.
